# @codenhub/error/react

## Classes

### AppErrorBoundary

```ts
export declare class AppErrorBoundary extends Component<AppErrorBoundaryProps, AppErrorBoundaryState>
```

An error boundary that catches what its children throw while rendering, normalizes it into an `AppError`, and renders `fallback` with it.

Like every React error boundary, it does not catch errors thrown in event handlers, in asynchronous code, or during server rendering; handle those with `attempt` or `attemptAsync`. An invalid `options` value throws from the boundary's render, to the boundary above it.

**Example**

```tsx
<AppErrorBoundary
  fallback={({ error, reset }) => <ErrorPanel message={error.message} onRetry={reset} />}
  onError={(error) => tracker.captureException(error.originalError)}
  resetKeys={[location.pathname]}
>
  <Page />
</AppErrorBoundary>
```

Catches exceptions generated in descendant components. Unhandled exceptions will cause the entire component tree to unmount.
